title: Ramdeobaba University Partners with QClairvoyance Quantum Labs to Establish Dedicated Quantum Software and Hardware Facilities - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Ramdeobaba University in Nagpur signed a two-year MoU with startup QClairvoyance Quantum Labs to build a Quantum Software Lab (browser-based QClair-Edu platform) and a Quantum Communication Hardware Lab (QKD/QRNG kits), with two embedded PhD-level Professors of Practice, under India's National Quantum Mission workforce push.

insights.claim: Ramdeobaba University and QClairvoyance Quantum Labs signed a two-year MoU to build a Quantum Software Lab and a Quantum Communication Hardware Lab, with RBU supplying space and QClairvoyance supplying cloud tools, photonic kits and faculty-in-residence.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows quantum education spreading to tier-2 Indian universities via startup-provided turnkey labs.

insights.claim: The partnership is tied to workforce development goals of India's National Quantum Mission, which aims to bridge theoretical physics teaching with commercial engineering skills.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: NQM-driven demand for education infrastructure is creating a services/B2B-education market for Indian quantum startups.

insights.claim: QClairvoyance will deploy two PhD- or postdoc-level specialists to RBU for 12 months as Professors of Practice, and will offer student internships with direct hiring pathways.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Startups are using academic partnerships as a talent-acquisition funnel amid scarce quantum talent.

insights.claim: QClairvoyance's QClair-Edu platform runs in standard browsers without local installs or GPU accelerators, supporting circuit design, Grover/VQE/QAOA testing and noise modeling.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Low-infrastructure simulators lower adoption barriers for cost-sensitive institutions, a scalable education product.
insights.locator: Bridging Algorithmic Simulation with Physical Optical Hardware

insights.claim: The hardware lab will use benchtop QKD and QRNG training kits so students can run physical key exchanges against classical eavesdropping simulations.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantum communication training kits are an accessible near-term hardware revenue niche versus full quantum computers.
